name: Giddel
overview: The name Giddel appears in the Old Testament as a designation for a group associated with the post-exilic community, specifically identified among the Nethinim, who were temple servants, as seen in Ezra 2:47, 56 and Nehemiah 7:49, 58. These verses list the children of Giddel alongside other families, underscoring their role in the restoration and service of God's house after the Babylonian captivity. Additionally, Giddel is noted as one of Solomon's servants, indicating a trusted position within the royal administration, which reflects God's providential ordering of His people in both worship and governance.
